t: Two balls roll. One gets there first. What is different about what it did?
Two balls cross the same floor. One arrives first. What made it faster?
Two balls travel the same distance. One takes less time. The difference has a name.
Two objects traverse equal displacements in different time intervals. The quantity that distinguishes them is fundamental.
sub: It covered the same ground in less time. That is what fast means.
Same distance, less time. That difference is what we call speed.
The ratio of displacement to time interval is speed — the scalar rate of motion.
Speed is |Δx|/Δt. The vector form, velocity, carries direction as well as magnitude.

question: Push the ball twice as hard. Does it go twice as fast?
If you push twice as hard, does the ball move twice as fast?
Double the push. Does the ball's speed double?
If the applied impulse doubles, does the resulting velocity double?
options: Yes, twice the push means twice the speed
No, it goes faster but not twice as fast
No, the push does not change the speed at all
stages.outcome: Yes, twice the push means twice the speed
note: Guess before you try it. The answer is hiding in the sim.
Predict first. The sim will tell you if you are right.
Form a hypothesis before testing. The prediction is what makes the result stick.
Predict the relationship between impulse and velocity before verifying empirically.

t: Try different pushes. Watch how the speed arrow grows.
Change the push and watch the speed arrow. Bigger push, bigger arrow.
goal: Reach the goal. Notice how the speed arrow changes with the push.
Reach the goal. Observe how the velocity arrow scales with the applied force.

t: Find the smallest push that still reaches the goal. Then halve it — what happens to the speed?
Determine the minimum push to reach the goal. Then halve the push and observe the velocity. Is the relationship linear?
goal: Reach the goal. The speed is whatever the push made it.
Reach the goal. Verify the impulse–velocity relationship.

t: How fast something goes is called its speed.
How fast you go is called speed. Speed is how much ground you cover in each second.
Speed is distance divided by time. The units are metres per second, written m/s.
Speed is the scalar rate of motion: |Δx|/Δt. Velocity is the vector form — speed with a direction.
sub: More push, more speed. Less friction, more speed.
Speed = distance ÷ time. More push means more speed; more friction means less.
A speed of 3 m/s means 3 metres every second. Friction reduces it; push increases it.
Velocity v = Δx/Δt. The impulse–velocity relationship is linear in the absence of friction; friction introduces a deceleration term.

t: Speed limits are about how fast you cover ground. The faster you go, the less time you have to stop.
A speed limit is a rule about distance per second. The faster you go, the longer it takes to stop.
Braking distance grows with the square of speed. A car at 60 mph takes four times as far to stop as one at 30 mph.
Braking distance d = v²/(2μg). The quadratic dependence is why speed limits are the single largest factor in road fatality rates.

q: How do we measure how fast something is going?
What is the scalar rate of motion?
options: How much distance is covered in a unit of time
How long something has been moving
why: Speed is distance divided by time. A ball covering 6 metres in 3 seconds has a speed of 2 metres per second.
Speed = distance ÷ time. It is the rate at which position changes. 6 metres in 3 seconds is 2 m/s.
Speed is |Δx|/Δt — the magnitude of the rate of change of position. Units: m/s.
Speed is the scalar magnitude of velocity: |Δx/Δt|. It quantifies the rate of position change without regard to direction.

q: Ball A goes 6 m in 3 s. Ball B goes 6 m in 2 s. Which is faster?
Ball A travels 6 m in 3 s. Ball B travels 6 m in 2 s. Which is faster?
Two balls travel 6 m. A takes 3 s, B takes 2 s. Which has the greater speed?
Two objects traverse 6 m. Object A takes 3 s, object B takes 2 s. Which has the higher speed?
why: Ball B covers the same distance in less time. Less time for the same distance means more speed.
Same distance, less time = more speed. B covers 6 m in 2 s (3 m/s); A covers 6 m in 3 s (2 m/s).
Speed = distance/time. B: 6/2 = 3 m/s. A: 6/3 = 2 m/s. B is faster.
v = Δx/Δt. v_B = 6/2 = 3 m/s > v_A = 6/3 = 2 m/s. Same displacement, shorter interval → higher speed.
